activities.anchor: which is why testing drives surveillance and preventive-surgery decisions
activities.caption: place the marker on the carrier risk
activities.name: oncBrcaPlace

config.prompt: The population baseline for lifetime breast-cancer risk is about 12%. Place the marker on the figure quoted for BRCA1 carriers:
config.why: Roughly 55–72% — five to six times baseline — with ovarian risk around 39–44%, which is why a positive test reshapes surveillance and preventive-surgery decisions. Hereditary cases are still the minority: about 5–10% of cancers run in strong single-gene families.

activities.caption: one line of the summary note over-unifies
activities.name: oncOneDiseaseSpot

config.prompt: A revision note on cancer classification — one line is wrong. Click it:
lines: Two tumours of the same organ can differ by a single driver and respond to entirely different drugs.
Hundreds of distinct diseases with distinct driver combinations sit under the one word "cancer".
So a single universal cure is a realistic near-term research goal.
The unifying abstraction is the evolutionary process, not the pathology.
config.correction: "The cure for cancer" is a category error: with hundreds of distinct driver combinations, progress arrives cancer-by-cancer, target-by-target — the evolutionary process is what unifies the framing, not the pathology.
config.why: A gain-of-function driver in one tumour and an amplification in another can make them therapeutically unrelated despite the shared organ.

activities.caption: pair each staging letter with what it records
activities.name: oncTnmMatch

config.prompt: The TNM system — pair each letter with what it records:

pairs.right: tumour size and depth of local invasion
whether distant spread has been documented

config.why: Staging precedes curative resection for a reason: what the disease can do matters more than how large it has grown.

activities.anchor: Size feels like the obvious measure of threat
activities.caption: true or false — reading a tumour's threat
activities.name: oncSizeJudge

statements.s: Millimetre for millimetre, size is the strongest predictor of outcome.
statements.why: Size is only the T of TNM; nodal spread (N) and distant metastasis (M) carry the prognostic weight.

statements.s: A small lesion can already carry metastatic competence in a minority clone.
statements.why: A tumour can shed vast numbers of cells per gram per day while still small — capability is a property of subclones, not of calipers.

statements.s: What makes a malignancy dangerous is what it can do — invade, travel, colonise — not merely how large it has grown.
statements.why: The cascade's capabilities, not the millimetres, set the prognosis.

activities.anchor: Judah Folkman's hypothesis became a drug class
activities.caption: which clone escapes the diffusion limit?
activities.name: oncAngioTrace

config.prompt: Two clones, same origin. One tips its angiogenic balance (VEGF up, thrombospondin down); one does not. Which curve keeps growing past the diffusion limit?
config.why: Beyond about a millimetre, oxygen and nutrients must arrive through new vessels — the clone that induces angiogenesis escapes the plateau. Bevacizumab and VEGF-receptor inhibitors exist to tip the balance back: normalising the supply, slowing growth, improving drug delivery — a capability exploited as a component, not a cure.

activities.anchor: Caveats to hold alongside the enthusiasm
activities.caption: walk the immune-era planning conversation
activities.name: oncImmunoBranch

config.root: Checkpoint inhibitors and cellular therapy are the immune era's two pillars. Walk a treatment-planning conversation.

start.text: A tumour tests PD-L1-positive. What does the biomarker actually predict?

choices.label: Which patients are more likely to benefit from a checkpoint inhibitor
choices.feedback: Biomarkers such as PD-L1 and mutational burden predict who — they do not promise.

choices.label: A guaranteed durable remission
choices.feedback: Only a minority of unselected patients benefit; the biomarker narrows the odds.

biomarker.text: Released brakes can hold remissions for years — and the physiological cost is autoimmunity: the same checkpoints protect normal tissue.

promise.text: Checkpoint inhibitors help a minority of unselected patients; biomarkers exist precisely because the response rate is not universal.

cart.text: For refractory CD19-positive leukaemias and lymphomas, cellular therapy hands the patient's own T cells a synthetic receptor — complete remissions since 2017, with cytokine-release syndrome as the toxicity to manage.

config.why: Unmasking the immune response buys durable remissions for a subset; biomarker selection and toxicity management travel with it.

activities.anchor: This is why honest screening claims are made in
activities.caption: drag between the flattering number and the honest one
activities.name: oncScreenCompare

config.prompt: One screening programme, two report cards — drag between them:

before.label: survival from diagnosis
before.text: Earlier detection stretches the clock from diagnosis to death without moving the death itself — and slow, indolent tumours that would never have harmed count as cured. The statistic rises; nothing is gained.

after.label: mortality
after.text: Deaths prevented per 1,000 people screened over 10 years — the measure that separates real benefit from bookkeeping, and the basis on which guidelines are risk- and age-stratified.

config.why: Survival-after-diagnosis can rise while mortality does not move; the ERSPC experience — modest benefit bought with substantial overdiagnosis — is why the honest claim lives on the right-hand axis.

config.prompt: A decade of evolution, condensed — drag the sequence into order:
items: An oncogenic KRAS mutation starts the clone in bronchial epithelium
A TP53 hit removes the apoptosis brake
Mutation bursts — chromosomal shattering, APOBEC — diversify the population into subclones
At roughly a billion cells (about a centimetre), new vessels are recruited and metastatic competence may exist in a minority clone
Symptoms and diagnosis arrive in the billions-to-hundreds-of-billions range — evolutionarily late
config.why: Which is why screening targets the interval, liquid biopsies chase the far smaller DNA-shedding signal, and treatment strikes hardest while the population is small and homogeneous.
